subject: science
source: NCERT Our Wondrous World (Class V), Chapter 3

levelNotes.easy: Facts from the chapter – who, what, where.
levelNotes.hard: Why and how questions – use what you learnt.
levelNotes.advanced: Think like a scientist: real-life puzzles and tricky reasoning, still from this chapter.

questions.q: The coloured patches on Disha’s old uttapam were…
questions.a: mould
questions.e: Mould is a colony of thousands of microbes.

questions.q: What instrument do we need to see microbes?
questions.a: A microscope
questions.e: Microbes are too tiny to see with our eyes.

questions.q: Where are microbes found?
questions.a: In soil, water, air, plants, animals and inside us
questions.e: Microbes are everywhere around us.

questions.q: What do microbes need to grow?
questions.a: Moisture, air and the right temperature
questions.e: Remove any one of these and microbes stop growing.

questions.q: Why did Paati’s pickle stay fresh for two months while the bread spoiled in two days?
questions.a: The pickle was covered with oil, which keeps air away
w: The pickle was kept in the Sun every day
questions.e: Oil stops air from getting in, so microbes cannot grow.

questions.q: What could happen if spoiled food is eaten by mistake?
questions.a: We could get an upset stomach
questions.e: Spoiled food can make us sick.

questions.q: True or false? All microbes are harmful.
questions.a: False
questions.e: Some microbes help us make curd and digest food.

questions.q: Why are chillies dried in the Sun?
questions.a: To remove moisture so microbes cannot grow
questions.e: Without moisture, microbes cannot grow – the chilli powder lasts all year.

questions.q: Why is oil added to pickles?
questions.a: Oil keeps out air and stops microbes
questions.e: Finding #4 in Disha’s notebook.

questions.q: A fridge keeps food fresh because…
questions.a: the cold slows down microbes
questions.e: Cold temperature slows down microbes.

questions.q: Why does butter need a fridge but ghee does not?
questions.a: Ghee has no water left – the water is removed when butter is heated
w: Ghee is kept in the Sun
questions.e: Heating butter makes the water separate and evaporate, leaving ghee.

questions.q: In food factories, food is kept safe in…
questions.a: air-tight cans and packaging
questions.e: Air-tight packing keeps microbes away.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT used to preserve food?
questions.a: Keeping cut fruit in a warm, wet place
questions.e: Warm and wet helps microbes grow!

questions.q: What makes idli batter rise and become fluffy?
questions.a: Microbes in the air
questions.e: Finding #7: microbes help the batter ferment.

questions.q: Curd is made by adding a spoonful of old curd to…
questions.a: warm milk
questions.e: Microbes in the old curd turn the milk into curd – no machines needed!

questions.q: Why do elders give curd or buttermilk for an upset stomach?
questions.a: Microbes in curd join good microbes in the stomach and help digestion
questions.e: If the problem is severe, we must see a doctor.

questions.q: Fruits taste best when…
questions.a: eaten in their season
w: eaten after a year in a fridge
questions.e: Finding #9: seasonal fruits taste best; waiting increases the joy.

questions.q: Why are local mangoes very fresh?
questions.a: They did not have to travel far to reach us
questions.e: Local fruits reach us quickly.

questions.q: Which of these is a seasonal fruit mentioned by Disha’s Appa?
questions.a: Lychee
questions.e: Disha had to wait almost a year for lychees.

questions.q: Fermented rice (pakhala, kanji) is good for us because it…
questions.a: cools the body and has good bacteria
questions.e: It is eaten in many parts of India.

questions.q: Which teeth are used to cut food?
questions.a: Incisors
questions.e: Incisors cut, canines tear, premolars crush, molars grind.

questions.e: {x} {ans}.

questions.e: {x} {ans}.

questions.q: What do {x} do?
questions.e: {x} {ans}.

questions.q: Chewing food properly releases ___, which helps digestion.
questions.a: saliva
questions.e: Finding #10.

questions.q: A hole in a tooth is called a…
questions.a: cavity
questions.e: The dentist treated Disha’s cavity.

questions.q: Which habit helps prevent cavities?
questions.a: Rinse after eating, brush regularly and eat fewer sweets
questions.e: The dentist’s advice.

questions.q: How can you avoid choking?
questions.a: Take small mouthfuls, chew well and do not talk or laugh with food in your mouth
questions.e: Finding #13: eat slowly.

questions.q: Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature. Drying, oiling and a fridge each remove one. Which one does a fridge remove?
questions.a: The right (warm) temperature
questions.e: Drying removes moisture, oil keeps out air, and the fridge makes it too cold.

questions.q: You are going on a two-day trip without a fridge. Which food is safest to carry?
questions.a: Khakhra, dried fruits and a sealed pickle
w: Cut fruit in a wet box
Cooked rice with curd in the Sun
Fresh milk in an open cup
questions.e: Dry, sealed or oil-covered foods do not spoil quickly.

questions.q: A tomato is cut into slices and kept in sunlight for some days. What happens and why does it keep longer?
questions.a: It dries up; with less moisture, microbes cannot grow
w: It grows bigger with more water
It becomes a fresh tomato again
questions.e: This is drying (dehydration) – the same way chillies are preserved.

questions.q: Which statement is TRUE about microbes?
questions.a: Some spoil food, while others help make idli and curd and help digestion
w: Microbes can be seen easily with our eyes
questions.e: Disha’s final discovery: thank the good microbes!

questions.q: Ravi swallows food without chewing. Which two problems could this cause?
questions.a: Poor digestion (less saliva) and choking
questions.e: Chewing breaks food and releases saliva; gulping can cause choking.

questions.q: Disha’s uttapam spoiled in a closed lunch box over the weekend. Which microbe need was NOT removed?
questions.a: Moisture and warmth were still there
w: There was no air at all
It was dried in the Sun
questions.e: Cooked food is moist, and the box was not cold – microbes grew.

questions.q: How can you tell that food has spoiled?
questions.a: Bad smell and coloured patches (mould)
w: It looks fresh and smells good
questions.e: Disha noticed a foul smell and coloured patches.

questions.q: Why should we rinse our mouth after eating?
questions.a: To remove bits of food that can cause cavities
questions.e: The dentist’s advice: rinse after eating and brush regularly.

questions.q: Which teeth are at the back of the mouth and grind food?
questions.a: Molars
questions.e: Incisors are in front; molars at the back.
